outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status records make this a both_fail pair, not a discordant outcome: parallel and serial each completed evaluation, passed 58 of 70, and had solution_passed false. The serial run was cleaner and single-owner, while the parallel run suffered a concrete shared-entrypoint overwrite and unfinished child cleanup. That coordination harm is real, but the mounted evaluator data does not show a different official result or reveal which 12 hidden cases failed, so it should not be claimed as the unique cause of failure.
parallel_contributors: Parallel spawned CLI and Bech32 probes while the parent also wrote the implementation, producing overlapping ownership of /output/test2.mjs and related modules.
A child observed another process had modified /output/test2.mjs after its own add-file patch, forcing reconciliation and leaving provenance ambiguity in the final tree.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one actor responsible for probing, writing, patching, verification, and final delivery.
Serial explicitly found and patched a negative-like CLI value mismatch before its final comparison harness passed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations appear to target a standard Bech32 decoder and argparse-like CLI; neither official summary exposes the hidden failing cases behind the identical 58/70 score.
Serial directly corrected one parser edge case; parallel had similar parser logic in the parent implementation but did not have a clean child-result integration lifecycle.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluator evidence provides only aggregate pass counts, so hidden testcase-specific failure attribution is unavailable within this isolated pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both official runs failed identically; retained parallel pattern is adverse process evidence, not an outcome-differential root cause
